annotation.title_clean: Embodied Digital Technologies: First Insights in the Social and Legal Perception of Robots and Users of Prostheses
annotation.title_en: Embodied Digital Technologies: First Insights in the Social and Legal Perception of Robots and Users of Prostheses
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Mandl, S.; Bretschneider, M.; Meyer, S.; Gesmann-Nuissl, D.; Asbrock, F.; Meyer, B.; et al.
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Two online experiments (N=459, N=433) examine how people perceive users of low- and high-tech prostheses and robots of varying anthropomorphism on competence, sociability and morality. Study 2 adds lay perceptions of robot legal personality and decision-making authority, giving first insights on whether anthropomorphic robots may need different legal treatment.
key_provisions_or_claims: Competence attributions to robots were negatively related to anthropomorphism; industrial robots rated most competent.
Participants were reluctant to attribute morality and sociability to robots.
Perceived legal personality and decision-making authority varied with anthropomorphism.
Users of bionic prostheses regain perceived competence while keeping warmth/morality attributions.
Findings inform robot design for acceptance and legal debate on e-person status.
